en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Acelaka Chapter 44.
The Training Rule on Being Concealed in a Secret Place.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyaputta, having gone to a friend’s house, sat down on a private, secluded seat together with his friend’s wife.
Then that man complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the noble Upananda sit down on a private, secluded seat together with my wife?”
The monks heard that man complaining, grumbling, and resenting [the matter].
Those monks who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and resented, saying:
"How can the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan son take a seat in private with a woman on a concealed seat?"... [and so forth]...
“Is it true, Upananda, that you sat down in private on a secluded seat with a woman?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him... [as before]...
"How indeed, foolish man, could you sit down in private on a secluded seat with a woman?
This, foolish man, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“Whatever bhikkhu should sit down in private on a concealed seat together with a woman, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever bhikkhu” means whichever such person... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Woman" (mātugāma) means:
A human woman, not a female *yakkha*, not a female *peta*, and not a female animal— even one born on that very same day, let alone one who is older.
"Together" means on one side.
"Secret" means the secret of the eye and the secret of the ear.
The "secret of the eye" means:
When the eye is being rubbed, or the eyebrow raised, or the head lifted, it is impossible to see;
as for the seclusion of the ear,
it is impossible to hear ordinary conversation.
A "concealed seat" means it is concealed by a wall, or a door-panel, or a palm-leaf mat, or a wicker screen, or a tree, or a pillar, or a granary—by whatever means it is concealed.
"Should sit down" means: [he sits].
If a woman is sitting and a monk sits down near her or lies down near her, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If a monk is sitting and a woman sits down near him or lies down near him, there is an offense of expiation.
Or if both are sitting or both are lying down, there is an offense of expiation.
If, perceiving her to be a woman, he sits down on a secluded, concealed seat with a woman, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, being doubtful as to whether she is a woman, he sits down on a secluded, concealed seat with her, there is an offense of expiation.
If, perceiving her not to be a woman, he sits down on a secluded, concealed seat with her, there is an offense of expiation.
If one sits down in private on a concealed seat with a female yakkha, a female peta, a paṇḍaka, an animal, or a woman who has assumed human form, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is not a woman and he perceives her as a woman, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is not a woman and he is doubtful about it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if one perceives what is not a woman as not a woman.
There is no offense if any other conscious man is present as a companion.
He stands, he does not sit;
indifferent toward the goal,
he sits with his mind directed elsewhere.
"Of one who is insane,
of a first-offender"—
thus ends the fourth training rule concerning secluded concealment.
